title: The World Cup Has Started. Here Is What Every Indian Fan Needs to Know.
excerpt: Forty-eight teams, three host nations, and Indian fans glued to screens at 12:30 AM. The biggest FIFA World Cup in history kicks off with Mexico versus South Africa in Mexico City.
body:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 kicked off on Thursday in Mexico City with the host nation taking on South Africa at Estadio Azteca. It is the biggest World Cup ever staged — 48 teams, 104 matches, 16 cities across three countries — and the first to be held jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

For the roughly five million Indians living across North America, this is not a television event. It is a neighbourhood one. Matches will be played in cities with some of the largest Indian-origin populations on the continent: the San Francisco Bay Area, Houston, Dallas, the New York-New Jersey metro, and the greater Toronto area. Group stage games run through June 27, with the final scheduled for July 19 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

## Watching From India

Indian fans had reason to panic just weeks ago. FIFA had not found a broadcasting partner in the country, leaving the fate of one billion potential viewers unresolved. The deadlock broke in early June when Zee Entertainment struck a deal covering the 2026 tournament and all FIFA events through 2034.

Matches will air live on Zee's newly launched Unite8 Sports network — four channels split between Hindi commentary (Unite8 Sports 1 and 1 HD) and English commentary (Unite8 Sports 2 and 2 HD). Streaming is available on the Zee5 app and website. A three-month "All Access + Sports" plan costs ₹799, covering the entire tournament.

The catch is timing. Most group-stage matches kick off between 12 PM and 10 PM Eastern Time, which translates to 9:30 PM to 7:30 AM IST. Indian fans will need to choose between sleep and football. The opening match, Mexico vs South Africa, begins at 3 PM ET — 12:30 AM IST on Friday, June 12.

## The Format Has Changed

This is the first World Cup to feature 48 teams, up from 32. Twelve groups of four replace the old eight-group format. The top two from each group, plus the eight best third-placed sides, advance to a new Round of 32 before the traditional knockout stages begin on June 28.

The expansion means more nations, more matches, and more marathon viewing for fans who follow every game. The group stage alone runs 17 days with up to four matches per day.

## Key Matches and Storylines

The United States opens its home campaign against Paraguay on Friday in Los Angeles, a high-pressure debut for a host nation that last reached the Round of 16 in 2014. Brazil, the perennial favourite, faces Morocco in East Rutherford on June 13 — a rematch of their 2022 quarterfinal clash that Morocco won in a historic upset.

Argentina, the defending champions, play Algeria in Kansas City on June 16. Lionel Messi has not confirmed whether this will be his final World Cup, but at 39, few expect him back in 2030.

Iran's group matches at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles carry a charge that goes beyond football. The Iranian diaspora in Southern California — the largest concentration of Iranians outside Iran — has organised protests against the Islamic Republic's representation at the tournament. FIFA's decision to prohibit pre-revolutionary Iranian flags in stadiums has intensified the backlash.

## Security at Scale

The FBI calls this the biggest security operation in American history. Director Kash Patel, the Indian-American law enforcement chief, has overseen preparations that include 300,000 background checks, a counterdrone training programme that has graduated 70 local police officers, and a joint operations centre staffed by police from 46 of the 48 participating nations.

The FBI's threat assessment for the tournament flags the ongoing Iran conflict as a potential trigger for protests and violent incidents across host cities.

## India Is Not Playing. Indians Are Watching.

India has never qualified for a World Cup since its lone appearance in 1950, when the team withdrew before the tournament. But the country's fan base is enormous. An estimated 100 million Indians watched the 2022 final between Argentina and France. Football viewership in India has grown steadily, fuelled by the English Premier League, La Liga broadcasts, and the rising popularity of the Indian Super League domestically.

For NRIs in US and Canadian host cities, the next five weeks offer something the cricket calendar rarely does: a global sporting event unfolding in their backyards. The group stage schedule puts matches in San Francisco, Houston, Dallas, and Toronto — all cities with significant Indian-origin populations.

The final on July 19 at MetLife Stadium is expected to draw a global television audience exceeding 1.5 billion viewers. Some of them will be watching from India, bleary-eyed, at 4:30 AM.
